diagnosis.mechanism: Chrome's IPC flooding protection allows 200 same-document navigations per ten-second window and silently drops the rest. The scripted sweep sends fragment activations, plus the full re-navigations it makes before an activation whose target is already the current hash, far faster than a reader can. Once the budget is spent, every later Enter leaves location.hash on the previous target until the window passes.
diagnosis.leadDisproved: The second link to the same target (activation 599) is not the cause. In the checker, activation 599 is preceded by a different hash, so it navigates normally. Activation 600 is the first one past the budget, and the hash stays on 599's target.
